patterns.what_worked: The engine half of the hold verdict went in cleanly: the grade map's ABSENCE of a hold_ok entry is the single gate for 'an attempt happened', so the no-points rule needed no second source of truth. Reading the client sources before designing the pull clock (no pull-timer API on any of the five branches) turned a guess into a documented constraint, and the projection could then be built on client-sourced cast times only.
patterns.what_was_hard: The spec's pin for the pull clock sits in tests/practice_ui_state.lua while the deliverable is main.lua's publication - the two readings (a live clock carried into the practice context vs a purely synthetic practice clock) were reconciled by publishing the live moment into the ctx AND letting a caller's own clock win, which satisfies both but needs the residual (the drill's grading basis can follow a real pull) written down. A concurrent warrior lane also landed mid-run and turned the harness red in files this lane never touched; the reds were left alone and recorded, not 'fixed' here.
patterns.skill_gap: The scope list named ten files but only six needed changes; diag.lua / practice_stats.lua / practice_progress.lua / tests/diag_state.lua were deliberately untouched, and saying so explicitly (with the reason) in the bench artifact is what keeps 'in scope' from turning into 'must touch'.
